question: Which metabolic and signaling responses to terpene exposure are reproducible, and which depend on cellular context or a specific target?

candidates.title: Transcriptome analysis of Botrytis cinerea in response to tea tree oil and its two characteristic components
candidates.use: Pure-compound arms for fungal exposure comparisons; preserve essential-oil mixture as a separate treatment entity.
candidates.notes: GEO family SOFT maps 15 samples to five arms (three each); raw reads in SRA SRP223939 and processed FPKM/GFF on GEO. No-treatment control lacks a matching solvent-only arm in the deposited metadata. Pure compounds and both mixtures remain distinct.

candidates.title: Genomic and Transcriptomic Study for Screening Genes Involved in the Limonene Biotransformation of Penicillium digitatum DSM 62840
candidates.use: Biotransformation/metabolic response; model treated-vs-time-matched control as primary contrast and 0 h as a separate time contrast.
candidates.notes: ENA BioSample titles map six paired-end runs to 0 h untreated (2), 12 h untreated (2), and 12 h R-(+)-limonene (2). Raw reads are available; no GEO processed count matrix identified. Use the time-matched contrast. Two replicates constrain variance estimation.

candidates.title: Linalool antifungal response in Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. radicis-lycopersici
candidates.assay: bulk RNA-seq; paired-end raw reads; associated proteomics
compounds: linalool; stereochemistry not resolved in checked source
candidates.use: Defined linalool-versus-vehicle fungal contrast; compare with bacterial linalool only at broad process level until orthology and toxicity context are resolved.
candidates.notes: ENA run report maps CK_1-3 and L800_1-3 to six paired-end runs. Long inhibitory exposure may capture secondary growth effects. Host tomato qPCR claims in the paper are separate from fungal RNA-seq.

candidates.title: Anti-listeria Activities of Linalool and Its Mechanism Revealed by Comparative Transcriptome Analysis

design.control: untreated control; vehicle handling to verify

compounds: linalool; source reports 95% material, stereochemistry not resolved in current evidence
candidates.use: Existing descriptive bacterial pilot. Retain as a separate kingdom/context stratum; do not call comparison with fungal linalool studies a direct replication.
candidates.notes: GEO series record documents only the 8 h contrast at 1x MIC; the article describes sampling at 4, 8 and 12 h, so do not assume all timepoints are deposited. GEO sample names show three replicates for each of the documented control (LM-DZ1-3) and treated (LM-FZC1-3) groups. Treatment at MIC may contain late/terminal stress effects.

candidates.title: Unveiling the Mechanisms for the Plant Volatile Organic Compound Linalool To Control Gray Mold on Strawberry Fruits
compounds: linalool; confirm stereochemistry and fumigation dose from methods
candidates.use: Potential within-species linalool time-course comparator; rich orthogonal phenotype evidence.
candidates.notes: Publication reports RNA-seq, proteome, ergosterol/membrane, mitochondrial potential, ATP and ROS results. Confirm public accession and raw data availability before ingestion.

candidates.title: PerturbSeqr signature catalog
candidates.assay: processed compound and genetic perturbation signatures from multiple resources
candidates.use: Search for cell-context-matched genetic perturbations of candidate signaling targets/pathway genes after target nomination. Not a terpene-exposure dataset and not a substitute for source-level validation.
candidates.notes: Catalog includes LINCS, Sci-Plex, Tahoe, RummaGEO, PerturbAtlas, CM4AI and other datasets. Inspect compound identity and underlying accession at signature level.

exclusion_rules: Do not treat terpene biosynthesis/chemotype/developmental expression datasets as exogenous terpene exposure.
Do not pool essential oils or plant extracts with pure-compound arms.
Do not treat non-terpene volatile organic compounds as terpene exposures.
Do not generalize fungal/bacterial exposure signatures to mammalian cell signaling.
Do not call pathway enrichment or a Perturb-seq signature proof of direct molecular target engagement.
